shared_elements: quadruped with legs and tail rendered in silhouette
carving executed on unpolished weathered stone in an outdoor excavation setting
flat, shallow relief with rounded modelling and plain background
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, smoothly modelled relief of profile animals — notably a quadruped with clearly delineated legs and a long sinuous body-form — cut into rough, weathered stone, and the technique (flat outlined silhouettes standing slightly proud of an unworked ground) is closely comparable. The decisive difference is organisation: A is a tall flat pillar with figures disciplined into stacked horizontal registers separated by a patterned band, whereas B's figures sprawl and overlap over the irregular curved faces of a boulder with no register system or shared orientation.
